verdicts.title: Recent advances on the log-rank conjecture in communication complexity
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: The log-rank conjecture is one of the fundamental open problems in communication complexity. It speculates that the deterministic communication complexity of any two-party function is equal to the log of the rank of its associated matrix, up to polynomial factors. Despite much research, we still know very little about this conjecture. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract discusses the log-rank conjecture relating communication complexity to the log of matrix rank, but makes no mention of Ehrhart theory or any 'Ehrhart semigroup rank' construction, so it neither supports nor refutes the specific conjectured linear correlation.

verdicts.title: Quantum communication complexity of linear regression
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Quantum computers may achieve speedups over their classical counterparts for solving linear algebra problems. However, in some cases -- such as for low-rank matrices -- dequantized algorithms demonstrate that there cannot be an exponential quantum speedup. In this work, we show that quantum computers have provable polynomial and exponential speedups in terms of communication complexity for some fundamental linear algebra problems \update{if there is no restriction on the rank}. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract focuses on quantum vs classical communication complexity for linear algebra problems like linear regression and Hamiltonian simulation, with no mention of Ehrhart theory, semigroup rank, or Boolean function communication rank. It shares only the broad 'communication complexity' vocabulary without addressing the specific conjectured relationship.
